title: Underlying sets of ring-valued inverse image, with its unit
statement: Let $h:T\to Z$ be a continuous map of topological spaces and $G$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $Z$. Write $|G|$ for its underlying sheaf of sets. Use the presheaf inverse images $h_p^{\mathrm{ring}},h_p^{\mathrm{set}}$, their sheafifications $h_{\mathrm{ring}}^{-1},h_{\mathrm{set}}^{-1}$, and adjunction units from [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. For each open $W\subseteq T$ there is a canonical bijection $$\beta_W:\varinjlim_{B\supseteq h(W)}|G(B)|\xrightarrow{\sim}\left|\varinjlim_{B\supseteq h(W)}G(B)\right|,$$ where $B$ ranges over the set of open neighbourhoods of $h(W)$ ordered by reverse inclusion and the right colimit is in commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. It sends each section representative to the same representative in the ring colimit, is compatible with restrictions in $W$, and is natural in $G$. Sheafifying these maps induces a canonical isomorphism of sheaves of sets $$\alpha_{h,G}:h_{\mathrm{set}}^{-1}|G|\xrightarrow{\sim}|h_{\mathrm{ring}}^{-1}G|,$$ natural in $G$, such that for every open $B\subseteq Z$ and $s\in G(B)$, $$\alpha_{h,G,h^{-1}B}(\eta^{h,\mathrm{set}}_{|G|,B}(s))=\eta^{h,\mathrm{ring}}_{G,B}(s).$$ No compactness, separation, nonemptiness or surjectivity assumption on $h,T,Z$ is required.

proof.text: For each open W, the costructured-arrow category indexing the presheaf inverse image is filtered: use structuredArrowOpEquivalence for Opens.map h and the existing cofiltered structured-arrow instance (finite intersections and the whole space). The forgetful functor from commutative rings preserves these filtered colimits, as in the Mathlib match of lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise. Therefore it preserves the pointwise left Kan extensions defining the inverse image. Define beta by whiskering the inverse of Functor.lanCompIsoOfPreserves with the sheaf-to-presheaf inclusion. This is already a natural presheaf isomorphism.

Naturality of beta with respect to the restriction W <= h^(-1)B moves beta before that restriction. Apply leftKanExtensionCompIsoOfPreserves_inv_fac_app at B to identify the composite of the set unit and beta with the underlying ring unit. Applying the ring restriction proves exactly the representative equation for every W, B, i, and s.

The general-site underlying-set sheafification comparison supplies preservation of sheafification by forgetting commutative rings. Apply the already proved canonical sheaf-pullback forgetful comparison to Opens.map h, and define alpha as its inverse. This construction is a natural isomorphism; it is set sheafification of beta followed by the canonical underlying-set sheafification comparison.

Expand alpha into sheafifyMap(beta) followed by sheafifyComposeIso. Naturality of toSheafify moves beta to the left, and sheafComposeIso_hom_fac identifies the remaining composite with the forgotten ring sheafification unit. This proves the required sheafification equation.

The unit equation for the canonical forgetful comparison sends the ring sheaf unit to the set sheaf unit. Apply alpha to this equation sectionwise at h^(-1)B and cancel the inverse comparison using its inverse-hom identity. The result is the required unit equation in the stated direction. All instances and equations apply to empty spaces and empty opens without extra assumptions.
